prompt: Create a production pixel-art TREE SPRITE SHEET for a simple top-down survival game, Outpost. FOUR separate complete standing trees in a clean 2x2 grid on a true transparent alpha background. Top-left OAK, top-right BIRCH, bottom-left YOUNG OAK, bottom-right DEAD TREE. SIMPLIFIED genuine low-resolution pixel art, each tree should look drawn on roughly a 64x96 or 80x112 pixel grid and enlarged with nearest-neighbor: clearly visible square pixels and blocky stepped contours. STRICT low detail: about 12-16 colors TOTAL shared palette, 3 green shades for foliage, 3 brown shades for wood, 2 cream shades plus dark marks for birch. Large readable rounded leaf CLUSTERS of solid color; no tiny individual leaves, no speckled texture, no moss noise, no photographic bark, no painterly shading, no subpixel detail. Simple clean outlines and a few blocky shadows. Oak full broad canopy and one continuous straight brown trunk with compact roots; birch lighter narrow canopy and one continuous ivory trunk with just a few dark horizontal marks; young oak smaller full green crown and thin straight brown trunk; dead tree clean gray brown bare trunk with a few thick angular branches and no leaves. Each trunk must be a continuous uncut natural trunk meeting the roots, no cut rings or seams while standing. Trunks remain visibly substantial enough to chop into logs. All trees have consistent overhead-left lighting and front-facing top-down game-prop viewpoint. Separate cells with ample transparent gutters; no objects touch edges or each other; no shadows outside roots; no UI, text, labels or borders. The result must be MUCH simpler and chunkier than realistic detailed pixel art, friendly readable game sprites with clear silhouettes, restrained muted meadow greens and warm wood colors. Transparent background, no checkerboard.
normalization: Shared 16-color palette; native 2px grid; complementary parts derived from intact masters
